lines:
Fixed and pushed as dfeeb56 (main -> origin/main). The previous fix (c3b528a) is superseded: its premise was wrong.

Root cause (now verified against upstream and independent reports, not inferred): on Linux WebKitGTK a clipboard image reaches the webview as a completely EMPTY DataTransfer - files empty, items empty, and `types` empty as well. WebKit bug 218519's PasteboardGLib path still drops the payload before the web content sees it (reproduced in Epiphany and by other Tauri apps at the same webkit2gtk versions), so no inspection of clipboardData can ever recover the image. The item-list fallback added in c3b528a therefore could not work, exactly as the user reported.

Change:
- desktop/src/chat/pasteImages.ts: `pasteIntent()` classifies a paste as `files` (webview exposed images), `ignore` (text or a copied file the default paste owns) or `native` (the webview exposed nothing at all). New `PasteClipboard.types`/`getData` fields make it testable.
- desktop/src/chat/clipboardImage.ts (new): reads the image from the OS clipboard through tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager, validates the RGBA buffer against width*height*4 and re-encodes it with a canvas as a "Pasted image.png" PNG File. Every refusal (no image, unsupported native format, no canvas) resolves to null so an empty paste stays a no-op.
- ChatComposer claims the paste synchronously before the async native read, and only when `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` is present; Chromium/WebView2 use the direct path and never touch the native clipboard.
- Rust/plugin: tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager 2.3.3 dependency, plugin registration, `clipboard-manager:allow-read-image` capability, @tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager 2.4.0.
- Extra feature the user requested in the same item: image drag-and-drop onto the chat input, for Linux and Windows. The main window sets `dragDropEnabled: false` so the webview receives HTML5 drops, the composer accepts dropped image files (new desktop/src/chat/dropImages.ts) with a drop highlight, and a document-level guard makes a drop anywhere else a no-op instead of navigating the webview.

Verification: tsc --noEmit clean; `pnpm test:chat` 238 passed (36 files) including the new pasteIntent/drop suites and the existing Linux item-list and text-paste regression tests; `pnpm build` ok; `cargo check` for desktop/src-tauri ok (pre-existing warnings only) and it validated the new capability. Disclosed limits: no display or OS clipboard exists in this environment, so the real OS paste/drop was not exercised end to end; the evidence is the platform behaviour (empty DataTransfer on Linux, documented and reproduced upstream) plus the composer-level tests. A dropped or pasted file the import path cannot store still reports "Choose PNG, JPEG or WebP images.", which is unchanged.

Reported bug: pasting an image from the OS clipboard into the chat is not working on Linux.

Platform: Linux (desktop app).

Expected: with an image on the OS clipboard, pressing the normal paste shortcut in the chat composer attaches that image to the message, the same way it already works for image files chosen through the picker.

Actual: pasting an image from the clipboard into the chat input does not work — nothing is inserted or attached.

Scope note: reported symptom as observed by the user; root cause is not yet established and must be investigated. Candidate area: clipboard paste handling in the chat composer (desktop/src/chat/ChatComposer.tsx) and the shared image import path (desktop/src/chat/images.ts); expected behaviour is described in docs/chat-images.md. Note that on Linux the clipboard may expose image data in several formats, so verify which formats the paste path actually accepts.

Acceptance: pasting an image copied to the clipboard attaches it in the chat composer on Linux, with a regression test covering the Linux clipboard formats actually reported by the platform.

data.title: Fix pasting an image from the clipboard into the chat on Linux
